drug_class: Insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) inhibitor / monoclonal antibody
purpose: Teprotumumab-Trbw is used to treat thyroid eye disease (also called Graves' eye disease), a condition where the muscles and tissues behind the eyes become inflamed and swollen. This can cause your eyes to bulge outward, feel painful, and cause double or blurry vision. This medicine helps reduce the swelling and can improve how your eyes look and feel.
how_it_works: Your immune system has a protein called IGF-1R that, when overactive in thyroid eye disease, causes inflammation and swelling behind your eyes. Teprotumumab is a special antibody — think of it like a targeted blocker — that attaches to this protein and stops it from sending the wrong signals. By blocking those signals, the medicine calms down the inflammation and helps the tissues behind your eyes shrink back to a more normal size.
common_side_effects: Muscle cramps or spasms, nausea, hair loss (usually temporary), diarrhea, fatigue or tiredness, dry skin, headache, changes in your hearing (such as ringing in the ears or muffled sounds), and high blood sugar levels. Tell your doctor if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious hearing problems, including hearing loss or ringing in the ears, which may sometimes be permanent — let your doctor know right away if you notice any changes in your hearing. It can raise your blood sugar, so if you have diabetes, your blood sugar will need to be monitored closely. It should NOT be used if you are pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby — use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 months after. Tell your doctor about all your medicines and health conditions before starting treatment. Infusion reactions (like flushing, fever, or fast heartbeat) can happen during the IV infusion.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV (intravenous) infusion directly into your vein at a clinic or infusion center — you cannot take it at home as a pill. You will typically receive 8 infusions total, given once every 3 weeks. Each infusion takes about 60 to 90 minutes. Your doctor or nurse will monitor you closely during and after each infusion.
